Module 7 · Persistence with MyBatis

MyBatis Rides Into Town

We are leaving the in-memory ranch and connecting Spring Boot to the real Postgres database. MyBatis lets you write the SQL yourself while it handles the repetitive JDBC plumbing.

Real Postgres@MapperScan@SelectXML mappersBound parameters
🎯 Understand annotation-based and XML-based MyBatis mappers.
🎯 Wire Spring Boot through MyBatis to the existing Sprint 3 schema.
Start the trailJump to lab
The cowboy rule: you write the SQL. MyBatis handles the saddlebags.
1 · From hardcoded data to the real thing

The data leaves the corral

Earlier modules used an in-memory repository. This module connects to the existing PaySprint Wealth Platform schema, with the same tables and seed data students already know.

Controller
→
Service
→
Mapper
→
Postgres
Key idea: a MyBatis mapper sits where the repository implementation sat. The rest of the application asks for data without needing to know the SQL details.

What MyBatis actually does

  • 🥾 You write the SQL.
  • 🐎 MyBatis executes it and maps rows to plain Java objects.
  • 🌱 Spring injects the generated mapper proxy as a bean.
  • 🪜 You stay above raw JDBC connection, statement, and result-set boilerplate.
2 · Setup, step by step

Saddle up Spring Boot for MyBatis

Dependencies

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.mybatis.spring.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>mybatis-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
  <version>3.0.3</version>
</dependency>

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
  <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
  <scope>runtime</scope>
</dependency>

application.properties

spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5433/mission
spring.datasource.username=postgres
spring.datasource.password=mission
mybatis.mapper-locations=classpath:mappers/*.xml
mybatis.configuration.map-underscore-to-camel-case=true

map-underscore-to-camel-case=true lets a column such as asset_class populate a Java field named assetClass.

3 · @MapperScan

Spring creates the mapper implementation for you

@MapperScan points Spring at the package containing mapper interfaces. At startup, Spring and MyBatis create dynamic proxy implementations and register them as beans.

@SpringBootApplication
@MapperScan("com.fidelity.leap.sprint6")
public class MissionServiceApplication {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    SpringApplication.run(
        MissionServiceApplication.class, args);
  }
}
🪜

The abstraction ladder

Raw JDBC sits lower on the ladder. MyBatis keeps SQL explicit but removes the connection, statement, and result-set ceremony.

4 · Style one

Annotation-based mapping

Best for short, obvious queries

public interface InstrumentMapper {

  @Select("SELECT ticker, name, asset_class, currency "
      + "FROM instruments WHERE ticker = #{ticker}")
  Instrument findByTicker(String ticker);
}

#{ticker} is a bound parameter. MyBatis turns it into a prepared statement parameter rather than concatenating user input into SQL.

QUIZ ALERT

Annotation mappers can return mapped Java objects. Short single-table queries are a natural fit for @Select, while complex joins are usually easier to read in XML.

5 · Style two

XML-based mapping

The Java interface stays clean

public interface HoldingMapper {
  List<Holding> findByClientId(int clientId);
}

The interface is only a contract. The SQL can live entirely in the XML file.

The XML file does the heavy lifting

<mapper namespace="com.fidelity.leap.sprint6.HoldingMapper">
  <select id="findByClientId"
      resultType="com.fidelity.leap.sprint6.Holding">
    SELECT c.client_id AS clientId,
           i.ticker,
           h.quantity
    FROM holdings h
    JOIN accounts a ON h.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN clients c ON a.client_id = c.client_id
    JOIN instruments i ON h.instrument_id = i.instrument_id
    WHERE c.client_id = #{clientId}
  </select>
</mapper>

The wiring is two string matches: XML namespace equals the fully qualified interface name, and XML id equals the Java method name.

6 · Bad version → test → fix

The missing ticker trap

Bad version

SELECT txn_type,
       quantity,
       price,
       txn_date
FROM transactions t
JOIN instruments i
  ON t.instrument_id = i.instrument_id

The join exists, but i.ticker is never selected.

What happens?

The query still runs. MyBatis maps the selected columns it has. The Java object's ticker field is left null or unset because MyBatis cannot invent a column that was never selected.

SELECT t.transaction_id,
       i.ticker,
       t.txn_type,
       t.quantity,
       t.price,
       t.txn_date
...

QUIZ ALERT

map-underscore-to-camel-case=true maps names such as txn_type to txnType. It does not add a missing ticker column to your query.

7 · Query result, not entity

A MyBatis result object is just a plain Java object

public class Instrument {
  private String ticker;
  private String name;
  private String assetClass;

  // getters and setters
}

No @Entity. No persistence context. No dirty checking. MyBatis populates fields from the query result and then hands you the object. Changing it does not automatically update the database.

Remember: the object is the shape of a query result, not a persistence-managed entity.
8 · The full ride

Controller → Mapper → Postgres → JSON

GET /instruments/AAPL
→
@RestController
→
InstrumentMapper
→
Postgres
→
JSON
@RestController
public class PortfolioController {

  private final InstrumentMapper mapper;

  public PortfolioController(InstrumentMapper mapper) {
    this.mapper = mapper;
  }

  @GetMapping("/instruments/{ticker}")
  public ResponseEntity<Instrument> get(
      @PathVariable String ticker) {

    Instrument instrument = mapper.findByTicker(ticker);

    return instrument == null
        ? ResponseEntity.notFound().build()
        : ResponseEntity.ok(instrument);
  }
}

Trail summary

🥾 MyBatis keeps SQL explicit.
🌱 Spring registers mapper proxies as beans.
🐎 Annotation and XML styles serve different query shapes.
🪜 Bound parameters protect queries without string concatenation.
🧩 Result objects are plain query shapes, not JPA entities.
⭐ The lab connects the service to real Postgres data.
